artifact.self_contained_problem:
Define the generalized Chebyshev-type polynomials $T_n(b,c)$ by $T_0(b,c)=1$, $T_1(b,c)=b$, and 
$$T_{n+1}(b,c) = b\,T_n(b,c) - c\,T_{n-1}(b,c) \qquad (n\ge 1).$$
For an odd prime $p$ and an integer $a$ coprime to $p$, let $\left(\tfrac{a}{p}\right)$ denote the Legendre symbol. Let $p$ be a prime with $p\notin\{2,5,19\}$. Prove or disprove the following statements.

(i) One has
$$\sum_{k=0}^{p-1} \frac{\binom{2k}{k}^2 \, T_{2k}(5778,1)}{1216^{2k}} \equiv \begin{cases}
4x^2 - 2p \pmod{p^2} & \text{if } \left(\tfrac{2}{p}\right)=\left(\tfrac{p}{5}\right)=\left(\tfrac{p}{19}\right)=1 \text{ and } p = x^2+190y^2,\\[2pt]
8x^2 - 2p \pmod{p^2} & \text{if } \left(\tfrac{2}{p}\right)=1,\ \left(\tfrac{p}{5}\right)=\left(\tfrac{p}{19}\right)=-1 \text{ and } p = 2x^2+95y^2,\\[2pt]
2p - 20x^2 \pmod{p^2} & \text{if } \left(\tfrac{2}{p}\right)=\left(\tfrac{p}{5}\right)=-1,\ \left(\tfrac{p}{19}\right)=1 \text{ and } p = 5x^2+38y^2,\\[2pt]
2p - 40x^2 \pmod{p^2} & \text{if } \left(\tfrac{2}{p}\right)=\left(\tfrac{p}{19}\right)=-1,\ \left(\tfrac{p}{5}\right)=1 \text{ and } p = 10x^2+19y^2,\\[2pt]
0 \pmod{p^2} & \text{if } \left(\tfrac{-190}{p}\right)=-1.
\end{cases}$$

(ii) One has
$$\sum_{k=0}^{p-1} (57720k+24893)\,\frac{\binom{2k}{k}^2 \, T_{2k}(5778,1)}{1216^{2k}} \equiv p\!\left(11548 + 13345\!\left(\tfrac{\ast}{p}\right)\right) \pmod{p^2},$$
where $\left(\tfrac{\ast}{p}\right)$ denotes the Legendre symbol $\left(\tfrac{-190}{p}\right)$.

(iii) Provided in addition that $p\ne 17$, one has
$$\sum_{k=0}^{p-1} \frac{\binom{2k}{k}^2 \, T_{2k}(5778,1)}{439280^{2k}} \equiv \left(\tfrac{-190}{p}\right) \sum_{k=0}^{p-1} \frac{\binom{2k}{k}^2 \, T_{2k}(5778,1)}{1216^{2k}} \pmod{p^2},$$
and
$$\sum_{k=0}^{p-1} (57720k+3967)\,\frac{\binom{2k}{k}^2 \, T_{2k}(5778,1)}{439280^{2k}} \equiv p\,\left(\tfrac{-190}{p}\right)\!\left(3983 - 16\!\left(\tfrac{-190}{p}\right)\right) \pmod{p^2}.$$
artifact.status_search_result: This is one of Z.-W. Sun's open conjectures on supercongruences involving sums with $\binom{2k}{k}^2 T_{2k}(b,1)$. Such conjectures (the "A-list" of Sun) remain largely open as of recent surveys; no published proof of this specific congruence (with parameters $b=5778$ at moduli $1216$ and $439280$) has been located.

status_evidence.title: Open Conjectures on Congruences (Z.-W. Sun)
status_evidence.snippet: Conjecture A84 lists supercongruences modulo p^2 involving sums of binomial(2k,k)^2 T_{2k}(5778,1) divided by 1216^{2k} and 439280^{2k}.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture is stated as an open conjecture in Sun's collection.
